column2: ENGLISH
Petition the Fire Lord
Send a petition to the Fire Lord: ask for royal patronage, or ask the throne to rebuke a rival of your house.
The Fire Lord may grant your petition or refuse it. Once every 5 years.

You wear the crown of the Fire Nation, but the throne of the Fire Lord has stood empty since the dispute began, and the court whispers that it is not truly yours. Your half-brother [atxf_camellia_champion.GetTitledName] holds the west with the Saowon behind him, and their stone camellia flies over more halls every season. Your mother's clan, the Keohso, rally to the winged peony.\n\nThe quarrel over Natsuo Island has become an excuse for both clans to arm. Every lord of the Fire Isles must now choose a flower.

The throne of the Fire Lord stands empty, and the man who sits nearest to it, [atxf_peony_champion.GetTitledName], is no more fit for it than you. The Saowon, the richest clan of the Fire Isles, stand behind you and their stone camellia. The Keohso cling to the winged peony.\n\nThe quarrel over Natsuo Island has become an excuse for both clans to arm. Every lord of the Fire Isles must now choose a flower.
Let the lords choose.

The quarrel between [atxf_peony_champion.GetTitledName] and [atxf_camellia_champion.GetTitledName] has reached our hall. Envoys of both the Keohso and the Saowon have come, each with gifts, each with promises. The winged peony of the Keohso, or the stone camellia of the Saowon?\n\nThose who back a side will be loved by it and hated by the other. Independent lords who back a side will march when their champion goes to war against the other.
The winged peony: we stand with [atxf_peony_champion.GetTitledName].
The stone camellia: we stand with [atxf_camellia_champion.GetTitledName].
This is not our quarrel.

A letter has come from Avatar [atxf_avatar.GetFirstName]. The Avatar writes that the quarrel between the Keohso and the Saowon will drown the Fire Isles in blood, and that the spirits do not care which flower wins. The Avatar expects the Fire Nation to settle its succession without war, and is watching.
We will heed the Avatar's warning.
The Avatar has no say in the affairs of the Fire Nation.
An envoy of the Keohso has come with a chest of gold and the winged peony on his sleeve. [atxf_peony_champion.GetTitledName] would be grateful, he says, if our house stood with the Peony.
An envoy of the Saowon has come with a chest of gold and the stone camellia on his sleeve. [atxf_camellia_champion.GetTitledName] would be grateful, he says, if our house stood with the Camellia.
Accept the gold, and the flower.
Send the envoy home.

The Camellia-Peony dispute is over, and the Fire Isles answer to us. But the clans that fought it, the Keohso and the Saowon, are still rich, still armed, and still proud.\n\nWe can break them, as no Fire Lord has dared before: strip their privileges and make every subject loyal to the throne alone. Or we can bind them to us in a compact, and share the realm with those who helped win it.
Break the clans. There will be one loyalty in the Fire Nation.
Make a compact with the clans.
What shall our petition to the Fire Lord ask for?
Royal patronage for our house
That the throne rebuke a rival of our house
Perhaps another time.
[From.GetTitledName] has sent a petition to the throne, asking for royal patronage: 50 gold to set the affairs of the house in order.
[From.GetTitledName] has sent a petition to the throne, asking you to rebuke [atxf_denounced.GetTitledName], a rival of their house. Granting it will please one house and anger the other.
Grant 50 gold.
Rebuke [atxf_denounced.GetTitledName].
Refuse the petition.
The Fire Lord has granted our petition: 50 gold, and the favour of the throne.
The Fire Lord has granted our petition and rebuked our rival before the whole court.
The Fire Lord has refused our petition.
So be it.
Our flower
The other flower
Broke the noble clans
Compact with the clans
Royal patronage
Refused my petition
Rebuked me before the court
The Clans Broken
The noble clans of the Fire Nation have been broken. Their wealth and levies answer to the throne, and their grudges to no one.
The noble clans of the Fire Nation have been broken. Their wealth and levies answer to the throne, and their grudges to no one.
Compact with the Clans
The Fire Lord rules with the consent of the great clans, and shares the realm's wealth with them. It passes to every Fire Lord while the Compact holds.
The Fire Lord rules with the consent of the great clans, and shares the realm's wealth with them.

Breaking the clans is the work of generations. Every year the throne grows stronger at their expense, and every few years you and your heirs will face a hard choice. At 100, the Absolute Throne passes to every Fire Lord after you.
While the Compact holds, every Fire Lord rules with the clans' consent, and their council will make demands every few years. Refuse twice, and the Compact shatters.

The clans have not forgotten that they once made Fire Lords. Breaking them is the work of generations, and it stands at [global_atxf_centralization.GetValue]/100.\n\nThe Keohso and Saowon still hold estates, offices and pride. Which of them shall the throne take this time?
Confiscate a great clan's estates.
Fill the offices with commoners, loyal to the throne alone.
Purge the Saowon.
Not yet.
[atxf_remonstrant.GetTitledName] has come before the court to remonstrate: the throne tramples rights the clans held before there was a Fire Lord. Other houses are watching how we answer.
Silence them.
Hear them out, and give a little ground.

It took generations, but it is done. The great clans are a memory: their estates belong to the throne, their offices to men and women who owe everything to the Fire Lord. From now on, the Fire Nation has one loyalty.
One nation, one throne.
Every Fire Lord from now on gains the Absolute Throne: tax +10%, levies +10%, +0.5 prestige a month.

A letter from Avatar [atxf_avatar.GetFirstName]. The Avatar has heard that the throne means to purge the Saowon, and demands clemency. The Saowon fought and lost, the Avatar writes, but their children did not. If the Fire Lord wants a nation loyal to the throne, it will not be built on a massacre.
We will spare the Saowon.
The Avatar does not rule the Fire Nation.
A living Avatar will demand clemency before the purge goes ahead.
No purges for 10 years.
The clan council invokes the Compact: the great houses have paid for the throne's peace, and now the throne must pay for theirs. They ask for 100 gold.
The clan council invokes the Compact: the great houses want a voice in the Fire Lord's council, not only in their own halls.
The clan council invokes the Compact: the great houses expect a royal match, a promise that a child of the throne will marry into a clan.
Pay the 100 gold.
Give the clans a seat on the council.
Promise the match.
The throne owes the clans nothing more.
A second refusal shatters the Compact: the Keohso and Saowon think 40 less of you for 20 years, and the throne turns to breaking them instead.

The Fire Sages have come to the palace, as they do for every new Fire Lord. They crowned your forebears, and they expect to be heard: in the temples, on the council, in matters of war. Others at court whisper that a Fire Lord who kneels to priests is no Fire Lord at all.
Revere the old ways.
The Sages serve the crown, not the other way around.
The Sages counsel patience with the clans: the project to break them falls back by 10.
With the Sages subordinated, the project to break the clans advances by 10.

The Absolute Throne
The great clans were broken generations ago. The Fire Nation has one loyalty: the throne.
The great clans were broken generations ago. The Fire Nation has one loyalty: the throne.
Clans on the Council
The great clans sit on the Fire Lord's council, as the Compact demanded.

Revered by the Fire Sages
This Fire Lord honours the Fire Sages and the old ways.
